note: Expectations for the synthetic corpus, fixed before any engine work (track 1d) and corrected after an independent review (version 2). Judged like a careful recruiter with the job-matching skill rubric. band = expected score range 0-100 (width <= 30; the effective score of an unscorable or absent job is 0). status = excluded (a decided violation) > unscorable (too little text) > scored. violations = decided hard-criterion violations (anue, country, dayRate). Availability is never decided: a start before the profile's availability is the check availabilityGap {days} (job start = explicit date, or the mail date for 'sofort'). checks = codes the engine should raise instead of deciding. mustOpen = case-insensitive substrings of must requirements that must NOT count as met. The IT profile's minimum day rate comes from the old fallback einsatzpraeferenzen.tagessatz_ab (950) because harte_kriterien has no min_tagessatz. Version 3 (matching track round 2): two more invented profiles, senior = sample_profile_senior.json (very senior interim finance and transformation consultant modelled on the job-matching rubric, with the permanent-role keys min_jahresgehalt, festanstellung_orte, festanstellung_remote_min and zielprofil_min_jahre) and sap = sample_profile_sap.json (SAP FI/CO consultant), and K41-K52 covering the new rules; all version-3 expectations were written before the engine change and are gated from ENGINE_VERSION 3 on (profileSince, since). New violations: salary, permanentRegion, tooJunior, formalOpen (only a mandatory, unattainable formal duty). New checks: salaryUnknown, permanentRegion (inferred permanent role), permanentRegionUnclear, anueRisk, seniorityUnclear.
